{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study systematically compares the concordance of animal model findings (specifically gene expression in response to inflammation and injury) with human clinical outcomes, providing quantitative measures of correlation (or lack thereof). It discusses translation rates and failures across multiple intervention-indication pairs, fitting the inclusion criteria.",
  "arm": "disease-biology",
  "arm_evidence": "The biological response to injury was analyzed on a molecular level, by looking into the regulation of about 5,000 human genes relevant to inflammation and by comparing them to the murine counterpart responses.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "sepsis-inflammation",
    "neurology-stroke",
    "infectious-disease",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study discusses inflammation, sepsis, endotoxemia, infection, ischemic stroke, and neurodegenerative diseases, and also mentions toxicology and pharmacology broadly.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study discusses findings from mouse models of inflammation, sepsis, and stroke, and also mentions toxicology studies using rodents and general animal use across biomedical areas.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly mentions '70-kg mice', 'rodent data', and 'murine counterpart responses', and also refers to a study comparing rodent and human toxicity.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study focuses on molecular-level analysis of gene regulation and inflammatory responses, which are secondary biomarkers, rather than hard clinical outcomes like mortality or survival."
}
